modules.title: Module 1: Lexical Search vs Semantic Retrieval

tasks.title: Keyword Search Limitations & Lexical Mismatch
tasks.instructions: Execute the lexical search step in 'labs/keyword_limitation_demo.py' or '00_lexical_vs_semantic.ipynb'. Query the policy corpus with 'distributed workforce policies' using exact keyword matching.

question.prompt: Why did the exact keyword search for 'distributed workforce policies' fail to match Policy_01_RemoteWork.txt?

options.text: The document file is corrupted or could not be read
Exact lexical matching requires verbatim token overlap; the policy discusses 'telecommuting' and 'remote working' instead
The lexical search algorithm automatically rejects documents with fewer than 1000 characters
The vector database rejected the query due to cosine distance cutoff

question.explanation: Lexical keyword matching relies strictly on verbatim token presence. When documents use synonyms such as 'telecommuting' or 'remote work', an exact search for 'distributed workforce' yields 0 matches because the literal tokens do not appear in the text.
question.hint: Check the terminal output showing 0 matching tokens found in the keyword search.

tasks.solution: Traditional keyword search requires exact character-sequence matches. Even though Policy_01_RemoteWork.txt covers distributed work rules, it uses the terms 'telecommuting' and 'remote working', resulting in 0 matches for 'distributed workforce'. Dense embeddings resolve this mismatch by representing concepts geometrically.

tasks.title: Semantic Similarity Advantage with Embeddings
tasks.instructions: Run the semantic ranking step. Observe how dense vectors generated by SentenceTransformers map queries and documents into continuous vector space, evaluating conceptual alignment via cosine similarity.

question.prompt: Which document was correctly retrieved at Rank #1 with the highest cosine similarity for 'distributed workforce policies'?

options.text: Policy_02_Security.txt
Policy_01_RemoteWork.txt
Policy_03_Expenses.txt
All documents had identical 0.0 similarity scores

question.explanation: Policy_01_RemoteWork.txt achieves the highest cosine similarity (~0.72) because the embedding model projects 'distributed workforce' and 'remote work' into nearby regions in latent space despite having zero exact keyword overlap.
question.hint: Inspect the 'Semantic Similarity Ranking' table in your script output.

tasks.solution: SentenceTransformers map semantically equivalent expressions ('distributed workforce' and 'telecommuting/remote work') to vectors pointing in nearly identical directions in 384-dimensional space, ranking Policy_01_RemoteWork.txt at #1.

tasks.title: Preserving Context with Chunk Overlap
tasks.instructions: Examine the boundary overlap demonstration in 'labs/chunking_lab.py' or '01_chunking_basics.ipynb'. Review the character spans at chunk boundaries.

question.prompt: What is the primary architectural purpose of setting a non-zero chunk overlap (e.g. 50 characters)?

options.text: To duplicate vectors in storage for disaster recovery
To prevent semantic context or statements from being bifurcated across chunk boundaries
To increase embedding batch calculation throughput on CPU
To compress the raw text before storing in SQLite

question.explanation: Chunk overlap ensures that conceptual statements spanning the boundary of a chunk are preserved in full context across adjacent segments, avoiding loss of semantic coherence.
question.hint: Consider what happens if a crucial noun-verb relationship is chopped right at the character boundary.

tasks.solution: Chunk overlap preserves continuity across split boundaries, ensuring queries matching boundary sentences retrieve complete information rather than truncated fragments.

tasks.title: Inspecting Embedding Dimensionality
tasks.instructions: Execute the embeddings lab step to load the local 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2' model and inspect the dimensionality of the generated dense embedding tensor.

question.prompt: What is the vector dimensionality (number of dimensions D per vector) produced by all-MiniLM-L6-v2?
question.explanation: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 projects arbitrary text into a 384-dimensional dense continuous vector space, providing a compact yet expressive representation ideal for CPU execution.
question.hint: Look for '✔ Vector Dimensionality (D): 384' in the script output.

tasks.solution: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 produces dense vectors of dimension 384. This compact size allows high-throughput similarity search on CPU while maintaining strong retrieval accuracy.

tasks.title: Evaluating Cosine Similarities in Latent Space
tasks.instructions: Run the cosine similarity step in 'labs/embeddings_lab.py' to compare the cosine similarity between Sentence 1 (RAG systems), Sentence 2 (Vector databases), and Sentence 3 (Sourdough bread recipe).

question.prompt: Why was the similarity between Sentence 1 (RAG) and Sentence 2 (Vector DB) significantly higher than between Sentence 1 and Sentence 3 (Sourdough)?

options.text: Sentence 1 and 2 had more characters in common
Their normalized dense vectors in 384D space have a small angular separation (dot product near 1.0)
The model applies alphabetical token prioritization
Sourdough is an out-of-vocabulary word that caused a tokenizer error

question.explanation: In geometric latent space, semantically related concepts are positioned with a small angle between their unit vectors, resulting in a cosine similarity approaching 1.0, while unrelated concepts are nearly orthogonal (~0.0).
question.hint: Cosine similarity measures the cosine of the angle between two multi-dimensional unit vectors.

tasks.solution: Cosine similarity measures directional alignment in latent space. Topics sharing conceptual domains (RAG and vector search) project into closely clustered angular directions.

tasks.title: Assembling the Grounded Prompt
tasks.instructions: Run 'labs/rag_pipeline_lab.py' to execute the end-to-end RAG pipeline: query embedding, vector lookup in ChromaDB, citation extraction, and grounded prompt synthesis.

question.prompt: How does injecting citation-bearing context chunks into the LLM prompt mitigate hallucination?

options.text: It permanently updates the foundational weights of the neural network
It constrains the generation task to closed-book reading comprehension grounded strictly in verified passages
It bypasses the softmax layer to force 100% deterministic outputs
It removes the requirement for a prompt template

question.explanation: RAG converts open-domain generative tasks into closed-book reading comprehension, constraining the LLM to ground its assertions in the explicitly provided context passages and cite source identifiers.
question.hint: Read the system instructions inside the 'Assembled Grounded Prompt for LLM' panel in your terminal.

tasks.solution: By providing deterministic context citations in the prompt, the model is instructed to answer solely using the verified evidence, drastically reducing speculative hallucinations.

tasks.title: FastAPI Microservice & Gateway Health
tasks.instructions: Launch the FastAPI RAG service using Uvicorn with loopback binding and root path: python -m uvicorn labs.api_app:app --app-dir /workspace --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --root-path /preview/8000. Then use the API Inspector tool or curl to query /preview/8000/health.

question.prompt: Why is the '--root-path /preview/8000' argument mandatory when running Uvicorn behind Nginx reverse proxy?

options.text: To allow Uvicorn to run on unprivileged port 8000 without root privileges
So that FastAPI's OpenAPI schema, Swagger UI (/docs), and redirects construct valid public URLs prefixed with /preview/8000
To enable cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) across all domains
To instruct ChromaDB to operate in read-only mode

question.explanation: Because Nginx strips the `/preview/8000/` prefix before proxying to loopback port 8000, `--root-path` informs the ASGI application of its public mount prefix. This ensures Swagger UI (/docs) and redirect responses build valid client-accessible links instead of broken root-relative links.
question.hint: Consider how the browser fetches '/openapi.json' when viewing documentation inside an embedded iframe.

tasks.solution: FastAPI uses root_path to construct relative URLs for interactive Swagger docs (/docs) and schema assets (/openapi.json), ensuring seamless operation behind reverse proxies.

tasks.title: API Query Execution & Recoverability
tasks.instructions: Switch to 'Full-Stack Testing Mode' or use the API Inspector to send a POST request to '/preview/8000/query' with payload '{"query": "How does HNSW use skip lists?", "top_k": 2}'. Inspect the returned JSON payload and practice port-8000 recovery.
commands: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/preview/8000/query -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"query": "How does HNSW use skip lists?", "top_k": 2}'

question.prompt: If the API Inspector reports 'Connection Refused (502 Bad Gateway / Network Error)', what is the primary diagnosis and recovery step?

options.text: Rebuild the entire container image
The Uvicorn backend process is stopped, crashed, or listening on the wrong interface; inspect the terminal logs and restart Uvicorn
Delete the ChromaDB database directory
Direct the browser to http://localhost:8000 on the host machine

question.explanation: Gateway 502 or Connection Refused means Nginx cannot reach 127.0.0.1:8000. Following spec Section 9 recovery guidance, check the terminal running Uvicorn, test local curl 'curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health', and restart the process.
question.hint: Check Step 1 in the API Inspector Troubleshooting & Recovery panel.

tasks.solution: Follow the port-8000 recovery workflow: 1) Verify Uvicorn is running in terminal, 2) Test local health with curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health, 3) Test gateway path http://127.0.0.1:8080/preview/8000/health.
